assertions.note: per TRADE, not per t: each trade_id must carry exactly two legs, opposite sides, equal quantity. Possible only because trade_id is a core field (gap G5, resolved 2026-08-22); the per-t form could be satisfied by two offsetting errors in one step
no order is filled, cancelled or expired for more than it was submitted for. Per order, not in aggregate — an aggregate identity cannot see one order over-consumed against another under-consumed
the sum of per-order residuals equals the terminal book depth: the per-order ledger and the mechanism's own snapshot agree
terminal snapshot only; the per-event form needs gap G1 closed
count of priced events outside the declared domain
the two engines emit the same events in a different order

Both engines average the same integer-valued prices, so the difference is zero in practice; the tolerance is kept non-zero only to avoid asserting bit-equality of a float division. Observed difference at fixture minting: 0.

min-lob-a computes the sample variance in two passes; min-lob-b from the sum of squares. On prices near 1000 the sum-of-squares form loses accuracy to cancellation: sum(x^2) ~ 4e7 against (sum x)^2/n ~ 4e7 for a difference of order 1e1, giving a relative error of order 1e-16 * 4e7 / 1e1 ~ 4e-10 in absolute terms. Observed difference at fixture minting: 3.82e-11 tick^2. The tolerance is set two orders of magnitude above the observed value and below any difference that would indicate a changed statistic.
